claims.text: The initial material is a NbMoCrTiAl refractory high-entropy alloy matrix containing in-situ formed TiC and Al2O3 particles.
The initial composite is produced through powder processing followed by spark plasma sintering.
The TiC- and Al2O3-containing NbMoCrTiAl composite has high compressive strength.
The TiC and Al2O3 particles are responsible for delivering the composite's high compressive strength.
The initial composite exhibits brittle or cleavage fracture behavior with little or no room-temperature ductility.
The initial NbMoCrTiAl-TiC-Al2O3 composite has high oxidation resistance.
Adding fine MoS2 particles before sintering and using extended ball milling or co-sintering will produce a uniformly dispersed, integrated lubricious phase.
MoS2 particles will preferentially decorate grain boundaries and phase interfaces in the modified composite.
The integrated MoS2 phase will establish continuous lubricating films during sliding.
At elevated temperatures, layered MoS2 will reorient at the sliding interface and thereby reduce friction and wear.
After MoS2 addition and during elevated-temperature sliding, the TiC- and Al2O3-reinforced alloy matrix will retain high mechanical strength.
After MoS2 addition, the composite will retain the oxidation resistance of the original material.
MoS2 addition will reduce the friction coefficient by approximately 20–30% relative to the lubricant-free baseline.
MoS2 addition will enhance wear resistance over a wide temperature range.
The mechanical strength of the MoS2-containing composite will remain near that of the original composite.
The lubricant-free NbMoCrTiAl-TiC-Al2O3 baseline lacks self-lubrication capability.
The beneficial self-lubricating effect of MoS2 will persist up to approximately 1000°C.
Above approximately 1000°C, thermal degradation or oxidation of MoS2 may undermine lubrication efficiency.
Uniform MoS2 dispersion and coherent interfaces are critical for avoiding degradation of mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator calls the modified material a 'dual-phase microstructure,' although the hypothesis retains a NbMoCrTiAl matrix, TiC, and Al2O3 and additionally introduces MoS2, implying more than two distinct phases or constituents.
